title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary Wallet Credit via Forged Mercado Pago Webhook
description: The Mercado Pago webhook endpoint (/api/economy/wallet/webhook/mercadopago) accepts incoming HTTP POST requests without validating the authenticity of the payload via HMAC-SHA256 signature (x-signature) or secret token. Additionally, the handler does not enforce idempotency or restrict token quantities to validated purchases. Any external actor can issue crafted webhook notifications specifying arbitrary user IDs and token quantities, crediting unbounded balances into user wallets without payment.
root_cause: processWebhook in src/modules/economy/mercadopago.adapter.ts does not verify webhook cryptographic signatures or transaction idempotency, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inflate wallet balances indefinitely.
intended_behavior: The Mercado Pago adapter should verify the cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 signature in the x-signature request header against the configured secret key, check that the transaction ID has not been processed previously, and validate that the credited token units strictly correspond to an authorized purchase.

trace.description: Receives unauthenticated HTTP POST requests on /wallet/webhook/mercadopago and passes raw body to adapter without signature verification.
Extracts payerId, tokenUnits, and paymentId from untrusted payload and invokes creditFromPurchase.
Forwards credit request to wallet repository.
Increments user wallet balance in SQLite database and logs wallet transaction without idempotency validation.

conditions.description: The endpoint /api/economy/wallet/webhook/mercadopago is publicly accessible over HTTP.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated external attacker on the public Internet.
instructions: Issue an HTTP POST request to /api/economy/wallet/webhook/mercadopago with status approved, target payerId, and desired tokenUnits.
Observe the HTTP 200 response returning success and the newly minted balance.
Query /api/economy/wallet/attacker-target-user to observe the fraudulent balance persisted in SQLite.
execution.expected_result: HTTP 200 OK with success: true and wallet balance credited by 999999 tokens.

remediation.strategy: Implement HMAC-SHA256 signature verification for Mercado Pago webhooks using a configured secret key. Require idempotency tracking via a processed payments ledger, and strictly validate token units as positive finite integers.

code_changes.fixed_code: export class MercadoPagoAdapter { processWebhook(payload: any, signatureHeader?: string): { processed: boolean; newBalance?: number; error?: string } { /* verify HMAC SHA256 against secret, check idempotency */ } }

likelihood.reason: Public endpoint requiring no credentials or specialized conditions to exploit.

impact.reason: Allows infinite fiat/token counterfeiting, breaking the platform's core closed-loop monetization model.

confidence.reason: Directly reproduced and confirmed via local HTTP requests against running runtime.

title: Private Chat DM History Exfiltration via Spoofed Header
description: The conversation retrieval endpoint (/api/chat/messages/:userA/:userB) relies on the client-supplied x-user-id HTTP request header to determine the identity of the requesting user. Because this header is untrusted and can be forged by any client, an attacker can set x-user-id to either userA or userB and retrieve the entire private messaging history between any two matched members.
root_cause: chatRoutes in src/modules/chat/chat.routes.ts does not authenticate callers via cryptographically signed session tokens, allowing callers to exfiltrate private conversations using spoofed x-user-id headers.
intended_behavior: The endpoint should resolve caller identity strictly from the verified JWT auth_token cookie and reject the request with HTTP 401/403 if the authenticated identity does not match either userA or userB.

trace.description: Receives GET request for /messages/:userA/:userB and reads requester identity from untrusted x-user-id header.
Performs authorization check comparing untrusted header value to path parameters userA and userB.
Queries and returns all private messages between userA and userB from SQLite.

conditions.description: Victim users have exchanged private messages in chat.

execution.attacker_perspective: External user or attacker who knows the user IDs of two conversation participants.
instructions: Identify the target user IDs (e.g. from public profile search or feed).
Send GET request to /api/chat/messages/<userA>/<userB> with header x-user-id: <userA>.
Receive full JSON payload containing confidential messages.
execution.expected_result: HTTP 200 OK returning all private messages between userA and userB.

remediation.strategy: Authenticate requests using the signed JWT cookie (auth_token). Reject any request lacking a valid JWT or where sub is not equal to userA or userB.

code_changes.fixed_code: const session = await getAuthenticatedUser(c); if (!session || (session.sub !== userA && session.sub !== userB)) return c.json({ error: 'Acesso não autorizado' }, 403);

likelihood.reason: Trivial to execute with any HTTP client by adding a single request header.

impact.reason: Complete compromise of intimate, private adult communications in violation of the platform's core confidentiality.

confidence.reason: Verified dynamically with reproduction harness returning sensitive conversation data.

title: Sender Impersonation in Private Chat Messages
description: The message creation endpoint (/api/chat/messages) accepts fromUserId and toUserId in the JSON body without binding fromUserId to the authenticated session user. While the system checks that fromUserId and toUserId are reciprocal friends, any third party can forge fromUserId and send messages on behalf of a friend, injecting fabricated messages into the private chat history.
root_cause: chatRoutes in src/modules/chat/chat.routes.ts does not bind fromUserId to the authenticated session identity, allowing third parties to inject forged messages impersonating other users.
intended_behavior: The sender ID should be forced to match the authenticated user ID from the verified session token, ignoring or rejecting untrusted client parameters claiming to be another user.

trace.description: Parses unauthenticated JSON body extracting fromUserId, toUserId, and text.
Checks reciprocal match between fromUserId and toUserId without verifying that the caller owns fromUserId.
Persists forged message into SQLite chat_messages table under the impersonated sender.

conditions.description: The impersonated sender and the recipient are mutual friends/matches.

execution.attacker_perspective: Any attacker who knows two mutual friends on the platform.
instructions: Target two accounts with mutual likes.
Send POST request to /api/chat/messages with fromUserId set to the sender to impersonate.
Observe HTTP 200 with saved message attributed to the impersonated sender.
execution.expected_result: HTTP 200 OK with message saved under impersonated fromUserId.

remediation.strategy: Extract user ID from verified JWT session. Force fromUserId = session.sub and reject mismatched body parameters.

code_changes.fixed_code: const session = await getAuthenticatedUser(c); if (!session) return c.json({ error: 'Não autenticado' }, 401); const fromUserId = session.sub;

likelihood.reason: Requires only knowing that two users are matched.

impact.reason: Enables malicious impersonation, stalking, and reputational harm in intimate adult conversations.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by executing message creation with spoofed fromUserId and verifying SQLite persistence.

title: Client-Controlled Privilege Escalation in Swipe Quotas, Jury Voting, and Story Publishing
description: Multiple API endpoints rely on client-supplied parameters to make authorization and monetization decisions. Specifically, /api/social/swipe checks isPremium from the request body to bypass the daily 30-likes limit; /api/community/jury/vote checks isAngel from the request body to permit voting in community disputes; and /api/community/stories checks isPremium and xpLevel from the request body to permit publishing erotic stories. Free and unverified users can supply these boolean flags to escalate privileges at will.
root_cause: Route handlers in src/modules/social/social.routes.ts and src/modules/community/community.routes.ts do not verify roles against server database records, allowing unprivileged users to declare privileged roles in request payloads.
intended_behavior: Privilege and subscription checks must query the authenticated user's record in the SQLite database (e.g. is_premium, is_angel, xp_level) rather than accepting self-declared status from client input.

trace.description: Accepts isPremium boolean flag from client request body.
Passes client-supplied isPremium to processSwipe quota validator.
Bypasses daily swipe rate limit when isPremium is true, recording like regardless of free tier quota.

execution.attacker_perspective: Free-tier user seeking unlimited likes, jury vote access, or story publishing.
instructions: Send POST requests with isPremium: true or isAngel: true in the JSON payload.
Observe successful execution bypassing monetization and governance boundaries.
execution.expected_result: Actions succeed without error despite user not possessing Premium or Angel status.

remediation.strategy: Query the authenticated user's actual database row (users table) to read is_premium, is_angel, and xp_level. Discard client-supplied role flags.

code_changes.fixed_code: const user = userRepository.findById(sessionUserId); if (!user?.isAngel) return c.json({ error: 'Acesso restrito' }, 403);

likelihood.reason: Any user can include the boolean parameter in HTTP requests.

impact.reason: Completely defeats monetization tiers and community governance integrity.

confidence.reason: Reproduced on live server with 35 consecutive swipes permitted via isPremium: true.

title: Client-Specified Token Reward Injection in B2B Treasure Claim
description: The B2B geolocated treasure claim endpoint (/api/community/treasure/claim) takes the tokenReward amount directly from the client's HTTP request body and credits it to the user's wallet without validating whether the treasure exists or what reward is officially configured. An attacker can claim millions of virtual tokens with a single request.
root_cause: communityRoutes in src/modules/community/community.routes.ts does not validate treasure reward amounts against server-side definitions, allowing clients to inject arbitrary token credit amounts.
intended_behavior: Treasure rewards should be defined server-side in a catalog or registry, awarding a fixed amount (e.g. 50-100 tokens) associated with the validated treasure ID.

trace.description: Receives POST request on /treasure/claim reading tokenReward directly from client body.
Passes client-supplied tokenReward to economyService.creditReward.
Credits user wallet balance by client-specified tokenReward in SQLite database.

instructions: Send POST request to /api/community/treasure/claim with an arbitrary treasureId and a high tokenReward.
Observe the HTTP 200 response reporting tokensAwarded: 5000000.
execution.expected_result: HTTP 200 with wallet balance increased by 5,000,000 tokens.

remediation.strategy: Define a server-side catalog of valid treasures with fixed reward amounts. Look up the configured reward by treasureId, ignoring client-provided reward values.

likelihood.reason: Trivial parameter tampering on public endpoint.

impact.reason: Enables unlimited unauthorized token generation, destroying the token economy.

confidence.reason: Tested and confirmed with 7,777,777 tokens credited on test instance.

title: Default PIN Authentication Bypass for Unconfigured Accounts
description: The identity service's verifyPin function falls back to checking inputPin === '1234' whenever the user record lacks a configured PIN (storedPin is null or undefined). Consequently, an attacker who supplies the user ID of any account created without a PIN can authenticate as that user by providing PIN '1234'. Furthermore, PINs are stored in plaintext in SQLite and lack brute-force rate limiting on the API route.
root_cause: verifyPin in src/modules/identity/identity.service.ts does not require an explicitly configured PIN, allowing attackers to authenticate as any user lacking a stored PIN using the hardcoded default PIN '1234'.
intended_behavior: If an account has no configured PIN, PIN authentication must be rejected. Valid PINs should be verified using cryptographic hashes and salted comparison, protected by rate limiting.

trace.description: Receives POST request to /login/pin with userId and pin.
Checks storedPin; when storedPin is null, falls back to inputPin === '1234' and returns true.
Signs and issues valid JWT auth_token for victim user ID and sets auth cookie.

conditions.description: Target user account has a null or unconfigured PIN in the database.

execution.attacker_perspective: External attacker targeting accounts created through automated onboarding or registration.
instructions: Discover or enumerate a target user ID.
Submit POST request to /api/identity/login/pin with PIN '1234'.
Receive HTTP 200 with signed JWT authentication token for the target victim.
execution.expected_result: HTTP 200 OK returning auth token granting full account access as victim.

remediation.strategy: Require storedPin to exist; reject authentication if null or undefined. Hash PINs with SHA-256 and salt before saving and verifying. Attach throttle middleware to rate limit login attempts.

code_changes.fixed_code: verifyPin(storedPin: string | null | undefined, inputPin: string): boolean { if (!storedPin) return false; return hashPin(inputPin) === storedPin; }

likelihood.reason: Default PIN is widely known and accounts without PIN are vulnerable immediately upon creation.

impact.reason: Complete account takeover of any user lacking an explicit PIN.

confidence.reason: Dynamically verified by creating a user with null PIN and acquiring a valid session token via PIN 1234.

title: Radar Check-in TTL Tampering and Headcount Poisoning
description: The check-in endpoint (/api/radar/checkin) accepts an optional expiresAt timestamp from the client request body. When provided, this timestamp overrides the computed TTL window (1h to 4h), allowing an attacker to set check-ins that expire years in the future. This permanently poisons venue headcount metrics on the anonymous radar.
root_cause: radarRoutes in src/modules/radar/radar.routes.ts does not enforce server-computed expiration bounds, allowing untrusted client input to override check-in expiration timestamps.
intended_behavior: The check-in expiration timestamp must be strictly computed on the server as Date.now() + ttlHours * 3600 * 1000, enforcing ttlHours between 1 and 4 hours and discarding any client-provided expiresAt value.

trace.description: Parses request body extracting spotId, ttlHours, and optional expiresAt timestamp.
Passes untrusted client expiresAt to checkinRepository.create.
Uses customExpiresAt to override server TTL calculation and stores future timestamp in checkins table.

execution.attacker_perspective: External user desiring to falsify establishment popularity or permanently tamper with radar data.
instructions: Send POST request to /api/radar/checkin with a timestamp 10 years in the future.
Query /api/radar/radar/spot-oasis to confirm the headcount remains incremented indefinitely.
execution.expected_result: HTTP 200 with check-in expiration set to the far future, permanently inflating activeCount.

remediation.strategy: Remove the customExpiresAt parameter from the API route. Compute expiresAt strictly on the server based on clamped ttlHours (1 to 4).

code_changes.fixed_code: const expiresAt = Date.now() + ttlHours * 3600 * 1000; const checkin = checkinRepository.create(userId, spotId, ttlHours, expiresAt);

likelihood.reason: Parameter is openly accepted by the existing route handler.

impact.reason: Corrupts real-time radar metrics and venue headcount data indefinitely.

confidence.reason: Verified dynamically by inserting a 10-year check-in and observing active headcount.

title: Non-Atomic Ephemeral Media Consumption and Persistent Storage on Disk
description: The ephemeral media repository (consumeEphemeralMedia) uses a two-step SELECT then UPDATE pattern without transactional atomicity. Two concurrent requests can read the sensitive media data simultaneously before the record is marked consumed. Furthermore, setting consumed = 1 leaves the sensitive media payload intact in the SQLite database indefinitely instead of shredding it upon consumption.
root_cause: consumeEphemeralMedia in src/modules/chat/chat.repository.ts does not use an atomic conditional update and fails to wipe media data upon consumption, allowing race conditions and permanent disk retention.
intended_behavior: Media consumption must execute an atomic conditional update (e.g. UPDATE ephemeral_media SET consumed = 1, data = '' WHERE id = ? AND consumed = 0) returning the data only if the update affected exactly one row, and immediately shredding the stored data on disk.

trace.description: Receives GET request for /media/:id and invokes consumeEphemeralMedia.
Executes SELECT query to check if item is consumed.
Executes non-atomic UPDATE setting consumed = 1 while leaving sensitive adult media unencrypted on disk.

conditions.description: Concurrent HTTP requests arriving within the database execution window.

execution.attacker_perspective: Recipient attempting to capture or replay single-view destructive media, or an attacker with database read access.
instructions: Issue concurrent requests to /api/chat/media/<media-id>.
Inspect SQLite database to verify data field persists after consumption.
execution.expected_result: Sensitive media content remains queryable in the SQLite database after consumption status is 1.

remediation.strategy: Perform atomic conditional update checking consumed = 0 and simultaneously overwriting data with a tombstone string. Return data only if 1 row was modified.

code_changes.fixed_code: const result = sqlite.run('UPDATE ephemeral_media SET consumed = 1, data = "[DESTRUCTED]" WHERE id = ? AND consumed = 0', [id]);

likelihood.reason: Race condition requires concurrent execution, but data retention on disk is 100% reproducible.

impact.reason: Defeats single-view privacy promise for destructive selfies, leaving sensitive adult images on server storage.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspecting SQLite table after consumption and finding sensitive payload still present.
